 # Discover local AI agents with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint - Microsoft Defender for Endpoint | Microsoft Learn
 
-Microsoft Defender discovers supported AI agents and their MCP servers after it observes agent activity on onboarded devices and surfaces them in the AI agent inventory and advanced hunting. An installed agent might not appear until Defender observes agent activity. To learn more about local AI agent discovery, see [Local AI agent discovery with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](local-agent-discovery-overview). For coverage by agent, operating system, and MCP server configuration, see [Microsoft Defender for Endpoint AI agent support matrix](ai-agent-support-matrix).
+Microsoft Defender discovers supported AI agents and their MCP servers on onboarded devices. It surfaces these agents in the AI agent inventory and advanced hunting. To learn how discovery works, see the [discovery overview](local-agent-discovery-overview). For agent and MCP coverage by operating system, see the [support matrix](ai-agent-support-matrix).
 
-In this article, you learn how to view discovered agents in the inventory, review their configuration and risk, explore their relationships with devices and identities, and investigate agent presence using advanced hunting.
-
-Note
+For process-based discovery, observing the agent's process running can be enough for an inventory entry. The user doesn't need to submit a prompt or have permission to use the agent's service. Discovery doesn't prove active use or successful access to an AI service.
 
-Local AI agent discovery on macOS is in preview.
+In this article, you learn how to view discovered agents in the inventory, review their configuration and risk, explore their relationships with devices and identities, and investigate agent presence using advanced hunting.
 
 ## Prerequisites
 
@@ -59,8 +57,19 @@ Before you can discover local AI agents on endpoints, make sure you meet the fol
 - Your environment is in the commercial cloud. Sovereign and national clouds aren't supported.
 - Your organization has a Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Plan 2 license. For more information, see Licensing.
 - Your devices are [onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](onboard-configure).
-- Your devices run a supported version of Windows or macOS, and Microsoft Defender Antivirus is updated with current monthly platform and engine updates.
-- Microsoft Defender Antivirus is running in active mode on your devices, with real-time protection enabled.
+- Your devices run a supported version of Windows or macOS and meet the minimum Defender version requirements in the following table.
+- Microsoft Defender Antivirus is running in active mode on your devices, with real-time protection enabled, except for the Windows and macOS VS Code extension inventory entries described in the following note.
+
+| Operating system | Minimum Defender version |
+| --- | --- |
+| Windows | Microsoft Defender Antivirus platform version `4.18.26090.9` (2609) or later. |
+| macOS | Microsoft Defender for Endpoint version `101.26072.0017` or later. |
+
+Note
+
+On Windows and macOS, agent inventory discovery for the VS Code extensions marked with footnote 1 in the [support matrix](ai-agent-support-matrix#ai-agent-discovery-support) uses an onboarded, running, and reporting Defender for Endpoint client. The client periodically collects installed extension data. This inventory collection doesn't require antivirus active mode or the extension to run. MCP server configuration discovery still requires antivirus active mode and real-time protection. This exception doesn't indicate runtime protection support. The macOS extension entries remain in preview.
+
+Keep Defender and its security intelligence up to date. On Windows, install current monthly platform and engine updates.
 
 You don't need additional deployment, configuration, or scripts beyond the device onboarding requirements. If the device meets all of the prerequisites, agent discovery begins automatically.
 
@@ -76,6 +85,18 @@ Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Plan 2 is the minimum license for local AI agent
 
 Microsoft 365 E5 and Microsoft 365 E7 both include Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Plan 2. If your organization has Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Plan 2 without Microsoft 365 E7 or Microsoft Agent 365, you can discover local AI agents, view the inventory, and query agents in advanced hunting, but the risk level, risk indicators, and security recommendations aren't available.
 
+### Permissions
+
+To view the local agent inventory with Microsoft Defender unified RBAC, make sure your role and its assignment include:
+
+- **Permission:** **Security operations** > **Security data** > **Security data basics (Read)**.
+- **Users:** Your account, or a Microsoft Entra security group that includes your account.
+- **Data source:** **Security for AI**.
+
+For role setup steps, see [Create custom roles with Microsoft Defender unified RBAC](/en-us/defender-xdr/create-custom-rbac-roles).
+
+To view the attack surface graph for discovered agents, your role must also include **Security posture** > **Posture management** > **Exposure Management (Read)**, with **Microsoft Security Exposure Management** selected as a data source.
+
 ## View local AI agents in the inventory
 
 1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Defender portal](https://security.microsoft.com/).

englishSummary.headline: Local AI agent discovery has updated detection and access requirements
englishSummary.summary: The documentation now states that observing an agent process can create an inventory entry without a prompt or service permission, and that discovery does not prove active use or successful access. It adds minimum Defender versions and unified RBAC permissions for viewing inventory and the attack surface graph.
englishSummary.adminImpact: Update Defender to the documented minimum versions and verify the required Security for AI and Exposure Management permissions for administrators who need to view this data.

 - **Exposure map**: Visual relationships between local AI agents, devices, identities, and the resources those identities can access, to help assess potential impact.

englishSummary.headline: Local AI agent discovery requirements are now more specific

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Defender: Expanded URBAC permission support for email content access
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Defender has expanded Unified role-based access control (URBAC) permissions for email content access to include alerts related to potentially malicious URL clicks. Security analysts with the appropriate permission can now preview and download emails from four alert types, ensuring consistent access across scenarios.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and why

We’re expanding Unified role-based access control (URBAC) permission support for Email & collaboration content: Emails associated with alerts in Microsoft Defender. This change provides more consistent email content access across alert investigation scenarios based on a user’s assigned permissions.

Previously, this permission applied to:

  • Email reported by user as malware or phish
  • Email reported by user as junk

With this rollout, the permission will also apply to:

  • A potentially malicious URL click was detected
  • A user clicked through to a potentially malicious URL

Rollout schedule

General Availability (Worldwide): Available now

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Security analysts who preview or download emails associated with the affected alerts

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Defender

What will happen

Security analysts with the required permission will be able to preview and download emails associated with these four alerts:

  • Email reported by user as malware or phish
  • Email reported by user as junk
  • A potentially malicious URL click was detected
  • A user clicked through to a potentially malicious URL

Access is based on the user’s assigned Email & collaboration content: Emails associated with alerts permission.

Action required and recommendations

Ensure that users who need to preview and download emails associated with these four alerts have the required Email & collaboration content: Emails associated with alerts permission.

Learn more

  • Permissions in Microsoft Defender unified role-based access control (RBAC) - Microsoft Defender XDR | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as usual for your organization.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Defender for Office 365: Changes to Unified RBAC permission mapping for Microsoft Entra Security Operator role
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft is updating the Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Unified RBAC mapping for the Microsoft Entra Security Operator role, removing default access to email threat policies and Tenant Allow/Block List. Rollout starts December 2026. Organizations must manually assign permissions if continued access is needed.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 3, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and why

We are updating the Microsoft Defender unified role-based access control (Unified RBAC) permission mapping for Microsoft Defender for Office 365 (Email & Collaboration). Currently, the Microsoft Entra Security Operator role includes the Authorization and settings\Security settings permission through the default Unified RBAC mapping. As a result, users assigned this role can view and manage email threat policies and the Tenant Allow/Block List.

To align access with documented Microsoft Defender for Office 365 role expectations and least-privilege principles, we are updating the default mapping so that Authorization and settings\Security settings (All permissions) is no longer included by default for the Microsoft Entra Security Operator role mapping for the Microsoft Defender for Office 365 workload. After this change, organizations that have Unified RBAC enabled and rely only on the Microsoft Entra Security Operator role for this access will need to manually assign the appropriate permissions or assign a role that includes those permissions.

Rollout schedule

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Rollout begins in early December 2026 (previously early November) and is expected to complete by mid-January 2027 (previously early December 2026).

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Organizations where both of the following conditions apply:
    1. Microsoft Defender XDR Unified RBAC is enabled, or will be enabled, for Microsoft Defender for Office 365 (Email & Collaboration).
    2. Users assigned the Microsoft Entra Security Operator role.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Defender for Office 365 (Email & Collaboration)
  • Microsoft Defender XDR Unified RBAC
  • Microsoft Entra ID

What will happen

  • The default Unified RBAC mapping for the Microsoft Entra Security Operator role will be updated to align with its documented Microsoft Defender for Office 365 scope and least-privilege principles.
  • When Unified RBAC is enabled for Microsoft Defender for Office 365, by default, the Security Operator role will no longer provide access to view, create, edit, or delete email threat policies, including anti-spam, anti-phishing, anti-malware, Safe Links, Safe Attachments, and preset security policies. The role will also no longer provide access to view, add, edit, or remove Tenant Allow/Block List entries.
  • This change applies only to Microsoft Defender for Office 365 when Unified RBAC is enabled. Tenants that have not enabled Unified RBAC are not affected.
  • Organizations that want operators to retain access can manually assign the appropriate Unified RBAC permissions, including Core security settings and Detection tuning, or assign a role that already includes those permissions, such as Security Administrator.
  • Other role mappings and existing Exchange Online PowerShell authorization are unchanged.

Action required and recommendations

We recommend that you:

  • Review users who are assigned the Microsoft Entra Security Operator role and determine whether they rely on that role to view or manage email threat policies or the Tenant Allow/Block List.
  • If continued access is required, assign an appropriate role or grant the required Unified RBAC permissions, including Core security settings and Detection tuning.
  • Update internal operational procedures, runbooks, and access-control documentation as needed.
  • Communicate this change to security operations teams and help desk staff.

Learn more

  • Activate Microsoft Defender unified role-based access control (URBAC) - Microsoft Defender XDR | Microsoft Learn
  • Create custom roles with Microsoft Defender unified role-based access control (RBAC) - Microsoft Defender XDR | Microsoft Learn
  • Map Microsoft Defender unified role-based access control (RBAC) permissions - Microsoft Defender XDR | Microsoft Learn
  • Permissions in Microsoft Defender unified role-based access control (RBAC) - Microsoft Defender XDR | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.
